raw_response:
I'm 55 now, farming these 7 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. My wife helps me, but our son works in a factory in Shijiazhuang — he sends money home, but he can't get leave for planting or harvest. So it's mostly the two of us. My back isn't what it used to be, but I know every corner of this land.

It's early October. The maize is harvested and dried. This year I got about 950 jin per mu — around 480 kg — which is decent. I sold most of it and kept some for feeding. Now I need to get the wheat in.

**Winter wheat:** I'll plant around October 10th. I save my own seed — I have about 300 jin in the grain jar, but I need maybe 350 jin for 7 mu. I'll buy 50 jin from the village supply shop for about 100 yuan. Lao Zhang down the road bought that new variety last year, but my seed has done fine for ten years, so why spend the extra money?

For fertilizer, I do what I always do. I buy four 100-jin bags of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind. That's about 50 jin per mu. I spread it and work it in before planting with my hand tractor. Then in spring, I topdress with urea: 20 jin per mu at green-up in March, and another 20 jin at jointing if the wheat looks a bit yellow. Last year I did this and got about 900 jin per mu. I hope for the same.

Irrigation costs keep going up — the electricity bill for the well makes my wife worry. For wheat, I'll water three times: once right after planting if the soil is dry, once before winter freeze, and once at jointing in April. If May rains are good, I won't water at heading. I'll spray herbicide once in the spring when the weeds come up. No insecticide unless I see aphids. I plowed after maize harvest and I'll harrow once more before planting. My wife and I can handle the wheat planting and most of the work. For harvest in June, I hire a combine — 50 yuan per mu — because the wheat has to come out fast.

**Summer maize:** After wheat harvest in early June, the window is tight — maybe five or six days. I hire two laborers for two days to help plant, 120 yuan per day each. I buy hybrid seed, about 3 jin per mu. I put down compound fertilizer at planting — about 35 jin per mu — and topdress with 30 jin of urea at the big trumpet stage in July. I'll irrigate twice if the summer is dry: once at big trumpet and once at flowering. Harvest is late September, mostly by hand and with the small thresher.

Money is tight. I'm spending about 3,400 yuan total on inputs for both crops. That's a big chunk of cash, but if the weather holds and I get 900 jin wheat and 950 jin maize per mu, we'll have enough to eat and some to sell. I'd rather not risk cutting back on fertilizer — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps.
